concepts.def: Step 3: be able to copy the action

walkthroughs.body_html:
Albert Bandura, Ross & Ross (1961) studied 72 nursery children.

Each watched an adult model behave aggressively or non-aggressively toward an inflatable Bobo doll.

Children later allowed to play with the Bobo doll imitated the aggression they had seen — including novel verbal attacks.

Bandura (1977, 1986) outlined four mediating processes.

1. Attention — notice the model.
2. Retention — remember the behaviour.
3. Reproduction — physically able to copy.
4. Motivation — anticipate reinforcement.

Vicarious reinforcement (Bandura 1965) — observed reward boosts imitation.

Bandura argued behaviour, personal factors and environment all influence each other — reciprocal determinism.

Self-efficacy (belief in one's ability) is a key personal factor influencing whether learned behaviour is enacted.
